name: MN-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+18 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent party
Fischbach holds a large fundraising and cash-on-hand advantage over Osberg
Prediction markets price Republican win probability around 96%
No public polling or expert ratings exist to challenge the fundamentals
model.rationale: This western Minnesota seat leans heavily Republican, incumbent Michelle Fischbach is running again with a roughly four-to-one fundraising edge, and markets price her near-certain to win. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican margin.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing a competitive race, or a major shift in the national political environment, would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 7th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of R+18. Republican incumbent Michelle Fischbach is seeking reelection after clearing her primary, and she enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage: about $1.3 million raised and $920,000 on hand, compared with roughly $335,000 raised and $114,000 on hand for Democrat Erik Osberg. No outside spending of note has materialized on either side.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert race ratings to consult, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 96 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong lean, incumbency, and the money gap points to a comfortable Republican victory, with only a small chance of an upset.
